trust_decision.summary: Reject a backup whose inner backup.json 'name' could escape the directory it is written to: validated when backup.json is parsed (util.read_backup) and again at the local agent's path derivation (CoreLocalBackupAgent.get_new_backup_path), with the new exception tolerated by the two readers.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'backup upload during onboarding'; that view forwards to UploadBackupView._post (http.py:182-200), where the uploaded *outer* filename is already rejected at manager.py:1008-1015, so an engineer reading only the summary starts there and sees a check that already exists.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/backup/upload (manager.py:1988) and websocket backup/generate with name= (manager.py:1797)
websocket backup/info and backup/agents/info (startup disk scan of the backup dir)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the shared parser is not where the report points (the upload handler already rejects unsafe outer filenames at manager.py:1009, so the inner name looks like trusted HA-written metadata), and that Supervisor installs and remote-agent paths are the Supervisor's or the remote server's business.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The startup scan must survive one unreadable backup: _read_backups catches a fixed set of exceptions per file, so the new exception has to be added there (and in the core reader/writer) or a single bad file makes async_list_backups raise and hides every backup from the UI.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Supervised installs: SupervisorBackupReaderWriter.async_receive_backup uploads the raw stream and returns details.name straight from the uploaded backup.json without ever running read_backup, so an unsafe inner name reaches every other agent's filename derivation.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Supervisor installs use the Supervisor's own backup engine, which is assumed to validate names; the report points at the Core reader/writer and the core local backup directory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other package: components/hassio reader/writer, then components/webdav and components/sftp_storage sinks

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Create route with an admin-chosen name (websocket backup/generate name=, or the name persisted through backup/config/update): suggested_filename feeds the remote agent path directly, with neither read_backup nor the local get_new_backup_path in that path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The name is chosen by an authenticated admin at creation, not by an uploaded file, and a remote storage path is the remote server's filesystem rather than the local backup directory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other packages: components/webdav, components/sftp_storage (client.py:223-226), components/aws_s3 and the other agents using the suggested_filenames idiom

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the adjacent code already derives a path from an attacker-influenced string; a maintainer refactoring temp-file naming to keep the friendly name would plausibly do it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new caller of suggested_filename (export/rename/import helper) that trusts the stored name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: suggested_filename is exported from the component (__init__.py:84-85) for every agent, so a new feature reuses it without the sink guard

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the Supervisor twin of the core filename derivation, built from backup_name in the create path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the hassio backend already duplicates core's filename logic; a guard added only to the core local agent leaves this copy open

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second LocalBackupAgent (container/NFS mount agent) overriding get_new_backup_path without the parent check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: LocalBackupAgent is an abstract base with a path hook, and storage backends are added per integration
